subject: Analytics migration & consolidation: pathways, timelines, and vendor tradeoffs
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Analytics migration & consolidation: pathways, timelines, and vendor tradeoffs

Team —

We have a renewal window coming up for a handful of contracts (Snowflake compute commitments, Looker licensing, and a smaller Metabase instance used by growth). Before we start formal negotiations, I want to converge on two things this week: (1) whether we pursue consolidation (single DWH + BI stack) or keep a split approach, and (2) the primary decision criteria (TCO, latency, admin effort, security/compliance fit).

I attached a first-pass TCO model (DWH_TCO_2027.xlsx) and a short RFP draft. Quick asks:
- Monica: can you run a delta on committed vs on-demand Snowflake spend if we shift 30% workload to BigQuery (rough sketch is fine)?
- Marcus: technical notes on migration complexity (Looker -> Metabase or Looker->Looker on BigQuery), and any blockers for our current ETL patterns.
- Laura: procurement timeline — earliest we can start negotiations and any blackout windows for finance?

Goal: a recommendation memo by EOD Thursday (18th). If consolidation is the path, we'll need stakeholder sign-off (Product, Growth, Security) and a procurement cadence to hit renewals.

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform & Infra Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DWH_TCO_2027.xlsx, RFP_DataWarehouse_2027.docx

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Analytics migration & consolidation: pathways, timelines, and vendor tradeoffs

Rishi —

I ran a quick sensitivity on the Snowflake commit vs moving steady-state ETL/adhoc workloads to BigQuery. High-level findings:

- If we shift 30% of current compute hours to BigQuery on flat-rate slots + reservation discounts, our projected monthly spend drops ~12-18% year-1 (includes network egress assumptions).
- Migration lift is front-loaded: estimated 2.5-3 engineer-months to refactor SQL/ETL tests + validation in prod-like staging (depends on how many UDFs we need to port).
- Looker licensing is the wildcard — if we migrate to BigQuery but keep Looker, we get a simpler transition but lose potential savings from switching to Metabase or an open alternative.

I've attached the updated TCO sheet (tab: delta_30pct). I'm flagging two procurement risks: our current Snowflake commit window closes 2027-03-25 for the next discount tranche, and finance needs 6 weeks for contract review if there are new commercial terms (e.g., reserved capacity across clouds).

I'll block time Wednesday to walk through the numbers.

— Monica
Sr. Finance Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DWH_TCO_2027.xlsx (updated)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 08:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Analytics migration & consolidation: pathways, timelines, and vendor tradeoffs

Rishi / Monica —

Technical quick notes (short version):

- ETL & schemas: majority of our pipelines are ANSI-SQL-compatible. ~20% of jobs use Snowflake-specific features (tasks + streams) and some JS UDFs used by one ML feature. Those will need rework or a translation layer.
- BI compatibility: Looker models can be ported, but LookML-to-Metabase is non-trivial; Metabase would require rebuilding explores/dashboards (no automated converter). Keeping Looker and switching DWH underneath (Snowflake -> BigQuery) is operationally simpler but licensing costs remain.
- Latency: for our OLAP patterns BigQuery with slot reservations performs similar to Snowflake for 95th pct when queries are parallelized; ad-hoc spikes may show higher p99 without autoscale.
- Security/compliance: both Snowflake and BigQuery support our KMS/HSM flows. Looker has the enterprise SSO integrations we use; Metabase would need an enterprise license+SAML work and additional audit log plumbing.

I attached a short tech note comparing migration complexity (Looker_vs_Metabase_tech_notes.pdf). Re: migration timeline: allow 10 weeks for a minimal viable migration (core reporting + ETL tests) + another 4-6 weeks for broad validation and dashboard rebuilds.

— Marcus
Staff Data Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Looker_vs_Metabase_tech_notes.pdf

From: Samir Patel <sam@datafoundry.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightleaf.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Analytics migration & consolidation: pathways, timelines, and vendor tradeoffs

Hi Rishi / Laura —

Thanks for the note. DataFoundry works with a number of customers doing Snowflake->BigQuery lift-and-shift plus Looker model refactors. High-level proposal:

1) 8-week migration sprint to move core ETL and reporting layer (team: 2 engs + 1 PM + 1 QA), fixed price: $92,000.
2) Optional dashboard rebuild service (LookML->Metabase) estimated at $28k per 50 dashboards (includes QA and UAT support).
3) Post-migration runbook + 30-day hypercare included.

We can provide references and an SOW draft. If you want, we can join a 30-min call Thursday morning to walk through scope and assumptions.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Director, Solutions
DataFoundry

Attachment: DF_Snowflake_BQ_SOW_v1.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightleaf.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 10:16:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Analytics migration & consolidation: pathways, timelines, and vendor tradeoffs

Folks —

Short calendar/contract items:
- Finance blackout: 2027-03-01 -> 2027-03-10 (quarter close prep). Avoid starting new commercial negotiations that require bespoke SLAs in that window.
- Snowflake renewal deadline for our current discount tranche: 2027-03-25 — need final commercial terms by 2027-03-15 to have legal & finance sign-off in time.
- If we engage a vendor (e.g., DataFoundry), procurement will need: SOW, vendor insurance cert, and a copy of their SOC / security posture. Expect 3 weeks for internal approvals (fast path) once docs are in.

Recommendation: run an internal decision memo after the Thursday sync (you suggested EOD Thursday). If we go consolidation, target an LOI to vendors by 2027-03-01 to allow parallel work on procurement paperwork and avoid the finance blackout.

— Laura
Head of Procurement
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <sam@datafoundry.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Analytics migration & consolidation: pathways, timelines, and vendor tradeoffs

Thanks everyone — quick readout + next steps: 

1) Alignment: majority lean toward consolidation onto a single DWH (BigQuery) and keeping Looker in the short-term if budget allows; Metabase as a contingency for growth-facing dashboards that need lower licensing costs.
2) Action items: 
   - Monica: finalize the TCO with 3 scenarios (status quo, partial shift 30%, full consolidation) and add net present value for 3 years (due Friday EOD).
   - Marcus: produce a migration-risk checklist and a prioritized dashboard list (top 40) for rebuild scope.
   - Laura: draft a procurement timeline and vendor pre-req checklist; request DataFoundry's SOC report and SOW (I asked Samir to share).
3) Vendor call: Samir, yes please join a 30-min vendor scoping call tomorrow (Fri 10:00 PT) — Marcus and Monica will be on.

I'll assemble the memo after Monica's numbers are in and circulate to Product & Security for sign-off.

Appreciate the quick turn here.

— Rishi
Head of Platform & Infra Strategy
Redwood Inference
